tex_content.html:
Theorem
[Global a priori maximum bound] 1. ch8:8.16\group ch08-generalized-solutions Under the hypotheses of Theorem 8.15 and condition (8.8), every subsolution (respectively, supersolution) satisfies egin{equation} \sup _\Omega u\leq \sup _{\partial \Omega }u^++Ck \qquad \left( ext{respectively, }-\inf _\Omega u\leq \sup _{\partial \Omega }u^-+Ck ight), ag {8.39} \end{equation} where $k$ and $C=C(n, u ,q,|\Omega |)$ are as above.
Proof

\sketch Subtract the boundary supremum. The weak inequality becomes

egin{equation} ag {8.40} \int _\Omega igl(a^{ij}D_j uD_i v-(b^i+c^i)vD_i u igr)\, dx \leq \int _\Omega (f^iD_i v-gv)\, dx \end{equation}

for admissible nonnegative $v$. Set $M=\sup _\Omega u^+$ and test with $u^+/(M+k-u^+)$. This bounds the $W^{1,2}$ norm of $w=\log ((M+k)/(M+k-u^+))$. A second transformed test shows

egin{equation} ag {8.41} \| w\| _2\leq C(n, u ,|\Omega |). \end{equation}

It also gives the weak inequality

egin{equation} ag {8.42} \int _\Omega igl(a^{ij}D_jwD_i\eta -(b^i+c^i)\eta D_iw igr)\, dx \leq \int _\Omega (\widehat g\eta +\widehat f^iD_i\eta )\, dx, \end{equation}

where $\widehat g=|g|/k+|f|^2/(2\lambda k^2)$ and $\widehat f^i=f^i/(M+k-u^+)$. Thus $w$ is a subsolution with uniformly controlled data. Theorem 8.15 bounds $\sup w$, hence $(M+k)/k$, uniformly. Apply the same argument to $-u$.

□
